ideas.title: A black hole in your beak
ideas.critique: This is the pocket black hole from round 1, reworded: a physics object that things react to. The new part is that the player carries it and it never pops, plus real lensing in the tracer. That makes it a playable tool and a showcase of light, not an event, but orbiting hats and petals is still the bubbles and hail shape.

ideas.title: The island by smell
ideas.critique: A simulated field that decides where every creature walks is a change to how the island works, not one more event. The visible drifting wisps and a wind turn that sends everyone round together is striking and unlike any earlier post. It overlaps the earlier 'air you can stir' pitch, but here the field steers behaviour, which that one did not.

ideas.title: Prices that move the island
ideas.critique: This is the island market again, now with the missing piece the critic asked for: prices that change where creatures crowd. Still, a board, a rich strutter and a crash are gags the island already uses. The emergent move from fishing to pebbles is the only part that is truly new, and it is hard to see in a still or a film.

ideas.title: Hybrids
ideas.critique: Inherited bodies that change the population over days are a different kind of change from any earlier post, with a traceable lineage from real chats. The risk is that it is more creatures and bodies, which caps it at 4 if shown as only more creatures. Mixed bodies from generated meshes also make it expensive and fragile. It scores well only if the inheritance and the family tree are the visible point.
